svg.aria-label: Schematic: imperfect sensor data in contested conditions feed a resilient model that produces a confidence-rated situational picture

g.text: Assured situational awareness from imperfect sensor networks
What this research sets out to do: keep producing a trustworthy picture when sensors fail, links drop and coverage is incomplete, and say how far
each part of that picture can be trusted.
In contested or degraded conditions, reports arrive
late, patchy or not at all.
One model takes the data exactly as they arrive.
A complete, confidence-rated picture that supports

incomplete, rather than treating gaps as an
layout of the area to estimate what

Aim of this pipeline: keeps producing
widens and the operator is warned.
Decisions in denied, disrupted, intermittent or limited (DDIL) conditions
need estimates whose confidence can be trusted, not just estimates
that are accurate when everything works. The approach is developed
on an open, unclassified urban sensor network that fails in the same
ways a deployed sensor network does.
Schematic, not to scale. Situational-awareness levels after Endsley (1995). Testbed: Newcastle Urban Observatory pedestrian sensors. Newcastle University PhD research, sponsored by Dstl.
